title: Plausible vs Fathom
description: Plausible Analytics vs Fathom Analytics — two leading privacy-first analytics tools compared on pricing, features, and performance.
verdict: Both are excellent privacy-first alternatives to GA4. Plausible tends to be slightly cheaper at lower traffic tiers and offers open-source self-hosting. Fathom offers hosted simplicity plus Fathom Lite for free self-hosting with fewer features.
quickAnswer: **Plausible** and **Fathom** solve the same core problem: simple, privacy-respecting website analytics without GA4 complexity. The choice usually comes down to pricing at your traffic level, whether you need self-hosting (Plausible open source vs Fathom Lite), and whether you want a managed hosted dashboard.
bottomLine: You can't go wrong with either for privacy-focused web analytics. Choose **Plausible** for lower hosted entry pricing and open-source self-hosting. Choose **hosted Fathom Analytics** for a polished managed experience at moderate traffic, or **Fathom Lite** if you want free self-hosting and can handle ops yourself.

faq.question: Are Plausible and Fathom both cookieless?
faq.answer: Yes. Both tools are designed to work without cookies and without collecting personal data, making them popular GDPR-friendly choices.

faq.question: Which is cheaper for a small blog?
faq.answer: Plausible starts at $9/month for 10K pageviews. Fathom starts at $15/month for 100K pageviews. For very small sites, Plausible is typically less expensive.

faq.question: Can I self-host either tool?
faq.answer: Plausible offers a self-hosted open-source edition. Fathom's hosted product (Fathom Analytics) is cloud-only, but Fathom Lite is a separate free self-hosted option with fewer features and no vendor support.

faq.question: Do both support custom events?
faq.answer: Yes. Both Plausible and Fathom support custom event tracking for goals like signups, downloads, and button clicks.
